Samir Patel: Prepare baseline perf test plan and request for sample prompts by 2026-02-09

header:
Date: 2026-02-05 | Start: 16:00 UTC | Duration: 46m
Attendees: Alex Rivera (Redwood AE), Samir Patel (Redwood SE), Maya Chen (NovaQube Head of ML), Jordan Ruiz (NovaQube Infra), Priya Nair (NovaQube Security)
summary: Exploratory discovery for NovaQube's inference plan. Discussion focused on reserved GPU sizing, tenancy/isolation needs for regulated data, burst strategy with hot pools, fallback to hosted models, and security requirements (KMS, audit logs, SOC2). Agreed to run a short POC baseline and share security documentation and pricing.
topics: reserved capacity sizing, isolation/tenancy, burst prewarm and hot pools, fallback routing, private deployment options (VPC/on-prem), encryption/KMS, SOC2/ISO compliance, SSO/SAML, observability and cost metrics
transcript:
[00:00] Alex (AE): Hey everyone thanks for joining, quick intros?
[00:07] Maya: Maya Chen, Head of ML at NovaQube, we run document intelligence for regulated clients.
[00:12] Jordan: Jordan RUiz, infra lead. We shepherd the infra and cloud controls.
[00:16] Priya: Priya Nair, security.
[00:18] Alex: Great, I'm Alex from Redwood, Samir is our systems engineer, he'll cover perf and ops.
[00:25] Samir (SE): Hi all, thanks for having us.
[00:28] Maya: Quick context — we're evaluating hosted vs dedicated vs private. Main ask: predictable latency for 200 qps peak, P95 < 250ms for short queries, and strict data isolation for some clients.
[00:40] Jordan: Also burstiness is big — two daily spikes where traffic increases 5x for about 20–30 minutes, plus ad hoc load during campaigns.
[00:48] Alex: Got it. When you say dedicated, are you thinking reserved GPUs with tenant isolation, or private deployment into your VPC?
[00:55] Maya: Initially reserved GPUs maintained by Redwood, so Dedicated. But we need VPC peering for logs and some data sync. Private on-prem is a later conversation.
[01:05] Samir: Okay. Couple clarifying Qs: what's your average request token length and typical sequence lengths during peak?
[01:12] Maya: Average 120 tokens, but some long documents are 1,200 tokens — those are async. For the 200 qps goal, most are short.
[01:20] Jordan: Cost is a factor, we're trying to avoid overprovisioning but also need guardrails so SLOs aren't violated.
[01:27] Alex: Makes sense. From experience we usually advise a hybrid: reserved pool sized for steady throughput plus a hotpool for prewarmed capacity to handle short bursts. Would that suit?
[01:36] Priya: How does isolation work? We need logical tenancy separation so client data never co-mingles.
[01:41] Samir: Redwood Dedicated offers tenant isolation at the inference pool level — you can have isolated pools per major customer. There's also network-level restrictions with VPC peering and private endpoints.
[01:50] Maya: Any noisy neighbor protections? We run few heavy rerank jobs sometimes.
[01:55] Samir: We have scheduling and cosine heuristics — essentially we can pin heavy jobs to specific nodes, and enforce QoS so interactive traffic uses low-latency lanes. There's also optional reserved cores for latency-sensitive routes.
[02:06] Alex: On billing — reserved is commit-based monthly with burst allowances. We'll send a few tiers.
[02:11] Jordan: For bursting do you use prewarm or dynamic spare capacity? What's the fallback if the hotpool is exhausted?
[02:18] Samir: Two primary mechanisms — hotpool prewarmed instances for sub-minute ramp and a routed fallback to compatible model variants on Hosted (lower commit cost) or burst nodes if available. We can configure automatic fallback policies.
[02:30] Maya: Is fallback to hosted acceptable for regulated customers?
[02:33] Priya: That's my concern — we can't send unredacted PII out to hosted environments.
[02:38] Samir: For those clients we recommend either strict on-prem/Dedicated-only pools or routing rules that block fallback for routes flagged as restricted. You can also set a fail-close behavior rather than fail-open.
[02:49] Maya: Good. About performance — can Samir walk through expected latencies for different GPU classes?
[02:54] Samir: Sure. For small seqs on A100-class reserved nodes, P95 around 120–180ms depending on batching. On H100-like infra we see mid-80s to 140ms. But this depends on batch sizes and KV cache reuse. For your short queries we can tune batching low to keep latency.
[03:14] Jordan: Batch tuning vs cost — any heuristics?
[03:17] Samir: If your traffic is highly concurrent and short, smaller batches keep latency low but raise per-token cost. For cost-sensitive endpoints we can enable continuous batching and prefix caching to reduce token compute without ballooning latency.
[03:30] Maya: We also need audit logs, KMS integration, and SSO/SAML for RBAC.
[03:36] Alex: On security — Redwood supports customer KMS for key wrapping, audit trails with per-request metadata, SAML SSO, and can provide SOC2/ISO artifacts. We'll share the security pack.
[03:47] Priya: Do you support HSM-backed keys? We need HSM for some clients.
[03:51] Samir: Yes, we integrate with common KMS providers and HSM options for Private deployments. For Hosted there's envelope encryption with customer-managed keys where available.
[03:59] Jordan: Network egress — we need to ensure logs forward to our SIEM without passing through public endpoints.
[04:04] Alex: VPC peering and private endpoints plus direct log shipping to your S3 via VPC support that path. We'll include the network checklist.
[04:12] Maya: What's typical ramp schedule for reserved capacity procurement? Lead times?
[04:16] Alex: For reserved pools, contractual lead time is usually 2–6 weeks depending on GPU availability and region. If you need faster, we can provision burst-capacity by using shared hot nodes for initial ramp.
[04:28] Maya: Okay. For the POC we want Redwood to host the models but guarantee no fallback for regulated routes, and run a peak simulation of 5x for 30 minutes to verify SLOs.
[04:38] Samir: Sounds good. We'll need a sample prompt set, and a traffic replay or synthetic driver. We'll provide a perf plan with expected metrics and the runbook.
[04:47] Priya: We may request an on-site or VPC-deployed audit later. Do you do penetration testing?
[04:53] Alex: Yes, we can coordinate assessments; we also have third-party pen test reports we can share under NDA.
[04:58] Jordan: Any recommended quantization/precision changes to lower cost? We run a lot of embeddings and price matters.
[05:04] Samir: For embeddings there are quantized pathways that are cost-effective. For generation, int8/4-bit quantization works for many models but we should validate for your quality bar. Redwood Optimize suggests quant profiles per workload.
[05:17] Maya: How do you measure quality regressions during model updates?
[05:20] Alex: We tie quality monitors to prompt sets and run nightly evals, alerting if token-level or semantic metrics drift. We'll demo the console but for the POC we'll set baseline evals.
[05:33] Maya: On price — our procurement will push back if the committed tier is larger than needed. Do you support mid-contract resizing?
[05:40] Alex: We have flexibility: some tiers allow monthly adjustments with pro-rated credits, others are annual commitments with change windows. We'll map options.
[05:47] Jordan: For your fallback routing, are there audit trails for when a request was routed to Hosted versus Dedicated? We need that for compliance.
[05:53] Samir: Yes, per-request routing metadata, decision logs, and tagging are available. It's surfaced in the console and exportable to your observability stack.
[06:03] Maya: Any known issues with KV cache invalidation for multi-tenant pools? We've hit cache thrash before.
[06:08] Samir: We can pin KV caches to tenant lanes or use per-tenant cache partitions; that avoids thrash at the cost of memory duplication. We'll propose configs in the POC plan.
[06:19] Priya: SLA question: what does your uptime guarantee look like for Dedicated?
[06:23] Alex: SLA depends on plan — Dedicated has higher SLOs, uptime commitments and credits. We'll include SLA matrix in the package.
[06:30] Maya: Great. I want to confirm people on this call will be involved in the POC.
[06:34] Maya: I'll own quality metrics, Jordan will run the infra checks, Priya will handle security signoff.
[06:39] Alex: Good. To recap — Redwood will send pricing tiers, security pack, and a POC perf plan. NovaQube will share prompt set and target SLAs and confirm dates for the run.
[06:50] Jordan: Proposed POC window next week Tuesday?
[06:53] Samir: We can do Tuesday morning UTC, we'll also bring a small ops runbook.
[06:58] Maya: Works for me.
[07:00] Alex: Anything else?
[07:02] Priya: One more — can you include a checklist for data residency and log retention?
[07:06] Alex: Yes we'll add that to the pack.
[07:09] Maya: Thanks everyone.
[07:11] Alex: Thanks — we'll follow up with action items.
[07:14] [End of recording]
questions: What are lead times for reserved pools?; How does fallback routing get audited?; Do you support customer-managed KMS/HSM?; Can we block fallback for regulated routes?
notes: Customer is sensitive to any cross-tenant fallback. Prefers Dedicated with VPC peering; POC to validate 5x burst. Security will require HSM/KMS docs and pen test reports. SE to propose cache partitioning and hotpool config. AE to provide pricing tiers and SLA matrix.
